label: Problem set 2
title: Problem set 2: Potentials and thermodynamics of cells
summary: Practice converting between emf and free energy, entropy, enthalpy and equilibrium constants, and handling reference-electrode scales and formal potentials.

intro.text: Chapter 2 links the cell emf to thermodynamics: dG = -nFE, dS = nF(dE/dT), dH = dG + TdS, and log10 K = nE0/0.05916 at 25 C.
Whenever a potential is quoted, remember which reference it is measured against; converting between scales means adding or subtracting the reference potential.

blocks.text: Chapter 2 links the cell emf to thermodynamics: dG = -nFE, dS = nF(dE/dT), dH = dG + TdS, and log10 K = nE0/0.05916 at 25 C.

blocks.title: Cell free energy from the emf

questions.question: A cell reaction transfers n = 2 electrons and has a standard emf E0 = 1.10 V. Using dG0 = -nFE0 with F = 96485 C/mol, calculate dG0 in kJ/mol.
For a one-electron couple with E0 = 0.30 V at 25 C, calculate log10 K for the reaction, using log10 K = nE0/0.05916.
questions.explanation: log10 K = (1 x 0.30)/0.05916 = 5.07, so K is about 1.2e5. The emf is a direct measure of the equilibrium constant.

questions.question: For a two-electron cell the emf changes with temperature at dE/dT = -5.0e-4 V/K. Calculate the reaction entropy dS in J/(K mol), using dS = nF(dE/dT).
questions.explanation: dS = 2 x 96485 x (-5.0e-4) = -96.5 J/(K mol). The temperature coefficient of the emf measures the entropy change.

questions.question: A cell reaction has dG = -190 kJ/mol and TdS = -43 kJ/mol at 298 K. Calculate dH in kJ/mol, using dH = dG + TdS.
questions.explanation: dH = -190 + (-43) = -233 kJ/mol. This is the heat that would be released if the reaction ran without doing electrical work.

questions.question: A potential measured as 0.530 V versus NHE is to be reported versus the saturated calomel electrode, whose potential is 0.242 V versus NHE. Calculate E versus SCE in volts (E_SCE = E_NHE - 0.242).
questions.explanation: E vs SCE = 0.530 - 0.242 = 0.288 V. Converting scales is just adding or subtracting the reference potential.

questions.question: The formal potential of the Fe3+/Fe2+ couple in a certain medium is 0.700 V. Using the Nernst equation E = E0-prime - (0.05916/1) log([Fe2+]/[Fe3+]), calculate E in volts when [Fe2+]/[Fe3+] = 10.
For a spontaneous cell reaction, the standard free energy change and the cell emf are related by:
questions.explanation: The emf is positive for a spontaneous reaction and the free energy change is negative, so dG0 = -nFE0.

questions.question: The standard hydrogen electrode is assigned a potential of zero at all temperatures.
questions.explanation: The NHE is the primary reference; its potential is defined as zero, and all other standard potentials are measured against it.

questions.question: Which quantities can be obtained from electrochemical cell measurements? Select all that apply.
options: The activation energy of the counter electrode reaction
questions.explanation: Cell emf gives dG, its temperature coefficient gives dS, and together they give K (and dH). The counter electrode reaction is not characterised by the cell emf.

questions.question: The formal potential E0-prime incorporates activity coefficients and other medium effects.
questions.explanation: Unlike the standard potential, the formal potential is measured in a specific medium and absorbs activity coefficients, complexation and ion pairing.

questions.question: A quasireference electrode (a bare metal wire) is acceptable only if:
options: It is calibrated against a known couple and its potential is stable during the experiment
It carries no current at all
questions.explanation: A QRE has an unknown potential, so it must be calibrated (e.g. against ferrocene) and must not drift during the measurement.

questions.question: A cell that is chemically irreversible cannot behave reversibly in a thermodynamic sense.
questions.explanation: If reversing the current gives different reactions, the cell cannot be driven along a continuous series of equilibrium states, so it cannot be thermodynamically reversible.

questions.question: A one-electron reaction has E0 = 0.300 V. Calculate dG0 in kJ/mol (dG0 = -nFE0).
A two-electron reaction has dG0 = -100 kJ/mol. Calculate E0 in volts (E0 = -dG0/(nF)).
At thermodynamic equilibrium of a cell reaction:
options: dG = 0 and the emf is zero
questions.explanation: At equilibrium the reaction has no further tendency to proceed, so dG = 0 and, since dG = -nFE, the emf is zero.

questions.question: A positive cell emf corresponds to a negative free-energy change and hence a spontaneous reaction.
questions.explanation: Since dG = -nFE, a positive emf makes dG negative, the thermodynamic condition for spontaneity.

questions.question: Which can shift the measured potential of an electrode in a real cell? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Complexation, ionic strength and the reference scale all shift the reported potential. The colour of the electrode is irrelevant.
